description.content: ⭐ Core endpoints

Calculate a full natal chart: planets, house cusps, aspects, sect, and angular data for a given birth moment. When the birth time is unknown, send timeUnknown: true instead of time and the response carries planets and aspects with houses, angles and sect set to null, plus a timeUnknown block giving the range the Moon covers that day. With ?lang= the response adds localized: planet, sign and aspect names in that language, keyed by the English names.

query.description: Adds `localized`: planet, sign and aspect names in this language, keyed by the English identifiers the response already uses. Without it the response is unchanged; `Accept-Language` alone does not add it.

Comma-separated dotted paths, relative to `data`, to keep in the response. A path is applied to every element of an array, so `planets.name` means the name of each planet. Paths that match nothing come back in `_fields_unmatched`; a list where nothing matches at all is a 400, because an empty object would be a confident wrong answer.

Round every non-integer number in the response to this many decimal places. Integers are left alone, because an id is not a measurement. Ecliptic longitudes ship with fourteen decimals by default; 2 is about a tenth of an arcminute.

Each room gets its bearing from the centre of the wall-aligned mandala, its 8, 16 and 32 sector, its mandala cell and deity, the share of each direction it covers, and the verdict and source /vastu/rooms gives; the door gets its pada and result. Findings come heaviest first with remedies, and the score is version 2: weighted by importance, with a band. Magnetic north needs the declination, walls on the diagonals need the facing side, and an L-shaped plan is warned about rather than averaged. description.content: Added as a part of security scheme: apikey

Chaldean planetary hours for a date and place: 12 from sunrise to sunset and 12 from sunset to sunrise, so an hour is rarely 60 minutes. `startHour` and `endHour` are decimal local hours. Send `atLocalHour` (decimal local time, e.g. 15.2 for 15:12) to have the hour containing it marked `isCurrent`; without it no hour carries the field, because the answer is cacheable and a flag from the server clock would be stale by the time it renders. `sunTimes.polarState` is `normal`, `polar-day` or `polar-night`, and in the two polar cases there is nothing to divide, so `hours` comes back empty with a warning saying why.

description.content: Rank cities against the astrocartography lines of a chart for one of the 19 life categories. Distance to a line is computed from the body hour angle and altitude rather than against a discretised polyline, so it is exact: the distance to a horizon line IS the altitude in degrees of arc, and a meridian line offset is the hour angle times cos(latitude). Supportive and challenging totals are returned separately with every contributing line and its distance, so a strong-but-turbulent city is distinguishable from an average one. Bundled GeoNames set of 34,028 places above 15,000 people. **Not geocoding**: a smaller town is absent from the ranking rather than ranked poorly, and an arbitrary place name cannot be resolved.

description.content: Added as a part of security scheme: apikey

Latitudes where a fixed star and a planet are angular at the same moment, which is how Brady tabulates a paran: not a place, a latitude. Twelve event pairs per star and planet (rise, set, culminate, anticulminate, minus meridian against meridian, which is a shared right ascension rather than a paran). Each row carries the houses of the technique in plain form: which body does what, the latitude, and the meridian where it happens at this chart moment. Solved on hour angles rather than by intersecting map polylines, so the latitude is exact rather than quantised to the polyline step. `horizon` selects the geometric horizon (default) or the apparent one at -34 arcmin, measured at about two degrees of paran latitude at mid-latitudes.

Tithi, karana, yoga and nakshatra carry `endsAt` (local ISO time with offset); `sunNakshatra`, `moonrise` and `moonset` (first after sunrise, disc centre on the horizon as panchangs count it; null when the Moon does not rise or set within 30 hours). `muhurtas`: Brahma Muhurta, Pratah and Sayahna Sandhya, Vijaya, Godhuli, Nishita, `durMuhurtam`, `amritKalam` and `varjyam` (lists), each `{ start, end }` in local ISO time. `chandrabalam` and `tarabalam`: from sunrise to the next sunrise, one entry per Moon sign or nakshatra with `from`, `until` and `favourableFor` (birth rashis or nakshatras), Chandrabalam also `ashtamaFor`. All null where the Sun does not rise.

Which of the nine gems to wear, from the sidereal lagna. Two schools are implemented: `lagna-lord` (default) prescribes the gems of the 1st, 9th and 5th lords as the life, lucky and benefic stones; `functional-benefic` classifies every graha by the houses it owns from the lagna, prescribes only for functional benefics led by the yogakaraka, and names the functional malefics as gems to avoid. Both reach the same three gems, because a functional benefic is a graha owning a trikona and the trikona lords are the 1st, 5th and 9th: the school changes the ordering, the role each gem carries, and the avoid list. The response always reports which one produced it. Coordinates are required, since the whole answer is derived from the lagna. Each gem carries its substitutes, day, finger, metal, weight range in ratti/grams/carats, and beeja mantra. Planet dignity is returned as context and does not change the list.

The Tajika annual chart for one year of life. Cast on the moment the SIDEREAL Sun returns to its natal longitude, which for an adult sits many hours away from the tropical solar return and therefore on a different ascendant: the gap runs 0.4 h at age 1, 3.3 h at 10, 7.0 h at 20, 12.5 h at 36 and 17.2 h at 50. Returns the year entry to the second, the sidereal annual chart, the muntha (the natal lagna advanced one sign per completed year) with its house and lord, Panchavargiya bala for all seven grahas (griha, uchcha, hadda, drekkana, navamsa, summed and quartered into Vishwa out of 20), the five office bearers a year lord is chosen from, and five sahams. The year lord comes back twice, because the sources disagree: `varshesha` follows the Hayanaratna, which requires an aspect to the annual ascendant before strength is consulted and carries the reason it chose; `varsheshaByStrength` is the modern shortcut of taking the strongest candidate outright. Pass `entryLatitude`/`entryLongitude` to enter the year somewhere other than the birthplace, which moves the ascendant and the houses but not the planets or the muntha. Coordinates are required.

A kundli card in one call: D1 lagna and the nine grahas with sign names, the Moon nakshatra and pada, the running Vimshottari maha and antar at `targetDate` (default now), and the Parashari yogas and doshas with a `present` list of the ones found. Each part is the same answer as its own route (/vedic/varga/D1, /vedic/dashas/vimshottari/antar, /vedic/yogas/parashara/full, /vedic/doshas/parashara/full). `latitude` and `longitude` are required; `time` is `HH:mm:ss` or `HH:mm`. `nakshatra.nameLocalized` is the name in the requested language (Devanagari for hi, the Cyrillic forms for uk and ru, the international transliteration elsewhere). 50 credits.

Co-lord rule for Scorpio (Mars+Ketu) and Aquarius (Saturn+Rahu): pick the OTHER if exactly one is in the sign, else higher absolute longitude. Default variant = K.N. {
  "ok": true,
  "data": {
    "horoscope": "Поточна енергія місяця підкреслює поєднання практичності та інтуїтивного підходу. Сонце у Діві (0,4°) дарує ясність мислення, а його **трин до Місяця у Козерозі** створює гармонію між внутрішніми відчуттями та зовнішніми діями. Це сприяє більш збалансованому сприйняттю реальності, дозволяючи вам впевнено планувати справи, не втрачаючи при цьому чутливості до власних потреб. Кон'юнкція Сонця з Меркурі в Леві підсилює комунікативну активність, а одночасний опозиційний аспект Сонця до Північного Вузла вказує на можливість переосмислення довгострокових цілей.

**Ключові дати та планетарні події**

- **23 серпня** – Сонце в кон'юнкції з Меркурі (розумові ідеї, важливі розмови).  
- **24 серпня** – Місяць у опозиції до Марса (емоційна напруга, потреба у самоконтролі).  
- **26 серпня** – Місяць квадрат до Нептуна (можливі ілюзії, важливо залишатися реалістичним).  
- **27 серпня** – Венера у секстилі до Юпітера (можливості у стосунках та фінансах).  
- **30 серпня** – Венера в опозиції до Сатурна (випробування в особистих зв’язках, потреба у відповідальності).  
- **31 серпня** – Уран у трині до Плутону (неочікувані прозріння, трансформація).

**Теми кожного тижня**

*Тиждень 1 (1‑7 серпня)* – Під впливом Меркурія в опозиції до Північного Вузла ваші думки можуть виявитися суперечливими. Це час, коли варто переглянути старі плани, відкинути зайве та сфокусуватись на нових напрямках. **Внутрішня гармонія** досягатиметься через письмову рефлексію та діалог із наставниками.

*Тиждень 2 (8‑14 серпня)* – Місяць у опозиції до Марса підкреслює емоційну напругу. Ви можете відчувати імпульсивність, тому важливо практикувати техніки розслаблення та встановлювати здорові межі. Працюйте над **самоконтролем** у стресових ситуаціях, уникайте конфліктів, які не несуть конструктивного результату.

*Тиждень 3 (15‑21 серпня)* – Венера в секстилі до Юпітера відкриває двері до нових можливостей у любові та фінансах. Це сприятливий період для спільних проєктів, романтичних ініціатив та інвестування в особистий розвиток. Однак опозиція Венери до Сатурна нагадує про необхідність **реалістичних очікувань** і планування довгострокових зобов’язань.

*Тиждень 4 (22‑31 серпня)* – Уран у трині до Плутону та Нептун у секстилі до Плутону активізують процеси трансформації та глибокого зцілення. Плутон у квадраті до Хірона підказує, що старі рани можуть знову з’явитися, проте це шанс їх переосмислити і звільнитися від обмежень. **Ліліт у трині до Хірона** підтримує інтуїтивне розуміння власних меж і потреб.

**Сфери фокусу**

- **Любов:** відкритість до нових знайомств (27 серпня), одночасно будьте готові до випробувань у стосунках (30 серпня).  
- **Кар’єра:** використайте ясність розуму (23 серпня) для планування проєктів; уникайте поспішних рішень під час емоційної напруги (24‑26 серпня).  
- **Фінанси:** можливості зростання через творчі інвестиції (27 серпня), проте дотримуйтесь бюджету та не піддавайтеся надмірному ризику (30 серпня).  
- **Здоров’я:** звертайте увагу на сигнали тіла під час Місяця в опозиції до Марса; практики дихання та легкі фізичні навантаження допоможуть зберегти баланс.  
- **Особистий розвиток:** працюйте над самосвідомістю через письмові практики (1‑7 серпня) і медитації, що підтримують процеси трансформації (22‑31 серпня).

Місяць пропонує вам поєднати аналітичний підхід з гнучкістю інтуїції. Використайте **трин Сонця до Місяця** як підґрунтя для гармонійного руху вперед, пам’ятаючи, що кожна можливість - це лише потенціал, який розкривається вашою активною участю та свідомим вибором. Нехай цей період принесе вам нові відкриття та внутрішнє зростання.",
    "disclaimer": "Це згенеровано ШІ виключно для розваги та саморефлексії. Не є медичною, юридичною чи фінансовою порадою. З відповідних питань зверніться до кваліфікованих спеціалістів.",
    "model": "openai/gpt-oss-120b",
    "language": "uk"
  }
}

The core of the Destiny Matrix per Natalia Ladini's method from a birth date: the personal square (pointA day, pointB month, pointC year digits, pointD bottom = A+B+C, pointE centre = A+B+C+D), the ancestral square corners, the sky (B+D) and earth (A+C) lines and the personal purpose, each with its arcanum. Numbers above 22 are reduced by summing digits. `karmicTail`, `loveLine` and `moneyLine` give the three arcana of each chain read from the centre outward, with `code` ("3-7-22"); the love and money channels share the `crossing` point. `ageScale` lists the 64 points from 0 to 78.75 years, clockwise from A in 1.25-year steps (the example shows the first 3). Ladini publishes no formulas; the chains and the scale follow E. Pribylova's book and the published calculators, which agree.

Create a new API key. Requires an internal or enterprise API key. Returns the generated key string once: only its SHA-256 is stored, so it cannot be retrieved later, only rotated. The plan comes from the account and is not accepted in the body. allowed_endpoints limits the key to a subset of the API: paths under /v1, exact ("chart") or a namespace ("embed/*"); omit it and the key may call everything the plan includes. credits_cap_cycle caps what this key may spend per billing cycle (0 parks it). A publishable key (origin_restriction.type "public", prefix pk_) is for page source, so it needs allowed_origins, credits_cap_cycle and allowed_endpoints: without any of them the request is refused with 400, and a pk_ key missing a bound is refused with 403 PUBLISHABLE_KEY_UNBOUNDED wherever it is used.

item.name: Rename a Key, Edit Origins, Budget or Scope

request.name: Rename a Key, Edit Origins, Budget or Scope

description.content: Rename a key, rewrite the origin list of a publishable key, set a per-key credit budget, limit the key to a subset of endpoints, or any combination. The class is fixed at creation: a pk_ key cannot become server-only, and a secret key cannot be given a list, so either request is refused with 400 rather than quietly rewritten. A new list takes effect at once and the key string does not change. credits_cap_cycle caps what this one key may spend per billing cycle, which credits alone do not, since they pool across the account; null clears it and a call over the cap answers 429 KEY_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED without falling through to overage. allowed_endpoints takes paths under /v1, exact ("chart") or a namespace ("embed/*"); null removes the limit and a call outside the list answers 403 ENDPOINT_NOT_IN_SCOPE. On a publishable pk_ key neither bound can be cleared: null for either is refused with 400.

item.name: Move a WordPress site onto an account key

request.name: Move a WordPress site onto an account key

description.content: Second half of connecting a site to an account. The owner picks a key on api.astroway.info/dashboard/connect, which sends the admin back to the site with a one-time `code`; the plugin exchanges it here, server side, sending its site key in `X-Api-Key`. The code lives 5 minutes; the same code from the same site key within 10 minutes returns the same answer, so a plugin that crashed before saving can ask again. The site key stops working 24 hours after the exchange. Errors: `400 INVALID_CODE`, `410 CODE_EXPIRED`, `403 SITE_MISMATCH`.

description.content: Compare up to five places for one birth chart as a multi-page A4 PDF (default) or live HTML (add `?format=html`). Per place: the relocated ascendant and midheaven with the signed shift from birth, **which planets changed house** (the substantive difference, diffed rather than left as two tables), every astrocartography line running within 300 km with its interpretation text, and supportive/challenging scores across the 19 life categories. With more than one place a side-by-side comparison leads the document. Relocation moves no planet: every body keeps its natal zodiac degree and only the houses and angles are re-cast, which the report states before anything else. Distance to a line comes from the body hour angle and altitude rather than from a discretised polyline, so it is exact. Coordinates are required per place and never defaulted. No AI narrative and no chart wheel, both on purpose: a wheel of the relocated chart reads as a second chart, and a narrative about a place is advice on where to live.

Your own credential for X-Provider. Never logged, stored or cached: it travels in a header because the request body is hashed into two cache keys, and a BYOK turn bypasses both caches in each direction. A provider error that quotes the key back is redacted before it reaches our logs or your response. Such a turn costs 5 credits instead of the endpoint price, and only when a completion actually ran on your key.

Optional model id, overriding the default for that provider. Defaults: openai → gpt-4o-mini, anthropic → claude-sonnet-4-5, google → gemini-2.5-flash, groq → openai/gpt-oss-120b, mistral → mistral-large-latest, openrouter → meta-llama/llama-3.3-70b-instruct, deepseek → deepseek-chat, together → meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct-Turbo.

header.description: Bring your own model key: the LLM provider that should run this completion. Send together with X-Provider-Key or the request is refused: a key with no provider bills us for tokens you meant to pay for, and a provider with no key would look like it worked. The endpoint is fixed per provider on our side and is never taken from the request. There is no fallback to our own chain: if your key fails you get the provider's status and message.

Your own credential for X-Provider. Never logged, stored or cached: it travels in a header because the request body is hashed into two cache keys, and a BYOK turn bypasses both caches in each direction. A provider error that quotes the key back is redacted before it reaches our logs or your response. Such a turn costs 5 credits instead of the endpoint price, and only when a completion actually ran on your key.

Optional model id, overriding the default for that provider. Defaults: openai → gpt-4o-mini, anthropic → claude-sonnet-4-5, google → gemini-2.5-flash, groq → openai/gpt-oss-120b, mistral → mistral-large-latest, openrouter → meta-llama/llama-3.3-70b-instruct, deepseek → deepseek-chat, together → meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct-Turbo.

🤖 Agent Platform endpoints

Tool definitions for an agent framework, generated from the live OpenAPI document, so the schema a model fills is the schema the endpoint validates. `format=openai` (default) returns `{ type, function }` objects you can spread straight into a chat completion; `format=anthropic` returns `{ name, description, input_schema }`. The objects carry nothing of ours: how to call each tool lives in a separate `executors` map keyed by tool name, because an unexpected key inside a vendor tool object is a 400 at their end. `select` chooses what to hand over: the curated starter set by default, `all` for the catalogue, `group:Vedic` for one area, `paths:/chart,/synastry` for an explicit list; `q` filters within that, `limit` caps it (default 32, max 128, which is the OpenAI ceiling). Nothing truncates silently: `totalMatched`, `totalAvailable` and a note say what was left out. No auth is embedded in a tool, so send X-Api-Key on the call itself.

query.description: Which vendor contract the tool objects follow. `openai` returns `{ type, function }`, `anthropic` returns `{ name, description, input_schema }`.

What to hand over: `starter` (the curated set, the default), `all`, `group:<tag>` such as `group:Vedic`, or `paths:/chart,/synastry` for an explicit list. An unknown path is named in `notes` rather than dropped.
Free-text filter applied within the selection, matched against path, summary, description and group.
How many tools to return. The ceiling is the OpenAI limit of 128 functions per request; models degrade well before it. Anything left out is counted in `totalMatched`.

request.name: Synastry score and cross-aspects (public, no key)

description.content: Compatibility score and the planet-to-planet aspect grid for two birth charts, served anonymously. Aspects come back sorted by orb, tightest first, so taking the first six gives the six an embed would show. `applying` is true when the aspect is still closing. `spheres` splits the same score by area of life: each sphere is the subset of cross-aspects that touch its body (identity: Sun, emotional: Moon, communication: Mercury, love: Venus, passion: Mars, commitment: Saturn), scored by the same model as `score`. An aspect between two sphere bodies counts in both. A sphere with no aspect has `score: null` and `count: 0`, not 50. The six keys are a closed list; new ones may be added, existing ones are not renamed. `strength` (0-100) is the weight the score is summed from (aspect type, the two bodies, orb), over its ceiling, an exact Sun-Moon conjunction; `tone` is the side of the score it lands on, `harmonious` or `challenging`, by the same rule (Venus-Mars counts as harmonious in any aspect). `chart1` and `chart2` are the two natal charts in the shape of POST /public/chart, so houses of one partner can be read against the other without two more calls; a partner with `timeUnknown: true` has no houses or angles. What stays behind a key: the per-aspect interpretations, the house overlay, composite and Davison charts, all of which the authed POST /synastry returns. Either partner may set `timeUnknown: true`; cross-aspects survive an unknown time because they are planet to planet. **This call costs 3 units** of the public rate-limit bucket rather than 1, because it computes two charts and the full matrix: 10 an hour on an undeclared address, 100 per declared site, 200 per address. The response carries `X-RateLimit-Cost: 3`. `localized` (follows `?lang=` / `Accept-Language`) carries display names beside the English identifiers, which stay as they are: `label` translated, `labels` and `spheres` as lookup tables keyed by the identifiers, `aspects` and `planets` keyed exactly as the `aspects` rows spell them.

description.content: All 78 unordered pairs of zodiac signs (each sign with itself included), each with the classical whole-sign relation: `same`, `sextile`, `square`, `trine`, `opposition`, or `aversion` for signs one or five apart, which classically do not see each other. `tone` follows Ptolemy (Tetrabiblos I.13): trine, sextile and same sign are `harmonious`, square and opposition `challenging`, aversion `neutral`. There is deliberately no 0-100 score: a pair of signs has no orb and no bodies for the synastry model to weigh, so any number would be invented. For a score, send two birth charts to POST /public/synastry. Static data, `Cache-Control: public, max-age=604800`, `Vary: Accept-Language`. `localized` (follows `?lang=` / `Accept-Language`) holds lookup tables from the English identifiers in `pairs` to display names: signs, relations, tones, elements, modalities. The identifiers themselves never change.

description.content: Sun-sign daily horoscope. No authentication, IP-rate-limited (30/hr). Cached per (sign, date, language); every response carries the `_footer` watermark. The text comes in `sections` (overview, love, career, health, finance, advice; null in the rare answer that missed one) and as `horoscope`, the same sections as plain paragraphs, without headings or markup. When the text cannot be written right now (`reason: "ai_unavailable"`) or is not ready within 15 s (`"ai_slow"`, it is still being written for the next reader), the answer is 200 with `X-AI-Cache: STALE` and `fallback: { reason, textDate, textLanguage }`: the most recent text for this sign in the requested language from up to two periods back, otherwise the English one. The computed fields are always for `date`. 503 `AI_UNAVAILABLE` only when no such text exists.

description.content: Reference prose for every closed set POST /human-design returns, in 21 languages: the five types (summary, strategy, signature, not-self theme), eight authorities, five definition kinds, twelve profiles, six lines, nine centres (theme, defined, open), 36 channels and 64 gates. Keys are the English identifiers the chart answer carries: `types[type]`, `authorities[authority]`, `definition[definition]`, `profiles[profile.profile]`, `centers[name]` with `defined` or `open`, `channels["lower-higher"]`, `gates[gate]`. Names are the same forms the localised chart uses. `gateLines[gate][line]` holds the 384 gate lines (English until a language's table arrives, flagged by `gateLinesLocalized`). `crosses[cross.name]` holds the 112 incarnation cross themes keyed by the full English name (e.g. `Right Angle Cross of The Sphinx`), each with `angle` (`RAC`, `JC`, `LAC`), `gates` (the Personality Sun gates that give it), a localised `name` and `text`; `crossesLocalized` is false where English stands in. `lang` is the language served; unknown codes resolve to `uk` like everywhere. Static data, `Cache-Control: public, max-age=604800`: fetch once per language.

description.content: Geocentric moon phase for a date (computed at noon UTC): deterministic, no AI, no birth data. `_footer` watermark. The English `phaseName`, `moonSign` and `sunSign` are the stable identifiers to match on and never change; `phaseKey` is the eight-phase key (new, crescent, firstQuarter, gibbous, full, disseminating, lastQuarter, balsamic). `moonDegree` is the degree inside `moonSign`, `distanceKm` the Earth-Moon distance, and `next` the UTC moments of the next four principal phases after noon UTC of `date`. `tithi` is the Vedic lunar day (1-30, 12 degrees of elongation each, geocentric), `voidOfCourse` the void-of-course spans that touch the UTC day (start, end, the sign the Moon enters). The moonrise-counted lunar day depends on the place and is not given. `meaning` and `keywords` are English; `localized` carries them with the phase and sign names in the requested language (a language whose translation has not arrived yet gets the English text).
